KEY MESSAGE 1...Anomalously warm low-level thicknesses and
dewpoints beneath strong ridging aloft will continue to keep 
temperatures well above normal with potential record breaking 
heat continuing through Saturday, with heat index values 
peaking at 105-110 deg today for most of the area, and possibly
again for srn zones on Saturday.

Today continues to have the strongest signal for the peak of 
this week's heat wave, with highs ranging 95-100 for the 
interior coastal plain, with low 90s coast. Thermal gradient 
should be strong enough to allow for fast seabreeze progression 
and thus preclude heat indices reaching 105 for portions of the 
immediate coast. The combo of hot temps well above 90 inland 
coupled with Tds well into the 70s bring heat indices 105+ once
again inland. Some locales may once again flirt with vals above
110 again, but not long enough or widespread for issuance of 
heat warnings. 

Saturday a cold front will begin sinking southward through the
area, but at the same time Td vals inc with moisture gradient 
tightening ahead of it, and with temps fcst to reach into the 
mid to possibly upper 90s in SWern zones, another day of heat 
indices 105-110 degrees is possible before expected numerous 
showers and storms ends the heat later in the day. Best chances 
to reach criteria are generally along and s of Hwy 70. A heat
advisory has been issued for this general area. Went below NBM
for Tds for tomorrow with today's obs showing NBM was overdone.
Have some heat advisory criteria AppTs in the grids all the way
up to the Nern tier despite the slightly lower HiRes blend Tds,
but opted not to go with a heat advisory this far north with
increasing clouds and shower and storm coverage likely to cut
down on the heat in this area earlier in the afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong upper level trough will develop off 
the U.S. East Coast over the weekend, and this will help drive a
strong cold front south through the Carolinas on Saturday and
Saturday night. Strong heating of a moist boundary layer ahead 
of the front should allow strong instability to develop from the
Mid-Atlantic south into North Carolina this afternoon and
evening. While some residual subsidence/capping was present
earlier beneath the ridge, especially across NC, guidance, and
now radar, shows a decent signal for convection developing 
north of the Albemarle Sound and into the Coastal Plain, and 
making a run towards the nrn zones late this afternoon and 
evening. Severe potential is there, esp north of Hwy 70 and 
best chances north of Hwy 264 with afternoon CAPE values in
excess of 3kJ/kg, and deep layer shear is above 25 kt. Main 
threat will be potential for damaging wind gusts, but strongest
storms may contain some hail as well. Severe watch is currently
set to expire at 2200edt though this may be extended in both
time and area.

On Saturday, the ridge will continue to get suppressed further 
south and west with less influence across the Carolinas. This 
plus increased forcing along the cold front should support an 
improved risk of deep convection, and less limiting factors, 
compared to Friday. PW's/TD's inc further and with lowering hts
aloft, instability will be very strong. In fact, vals will be
well above the avg max for first week of September according to
the KMHX sounding climatology, with ML CAPE vals advertised by 
the 03/12Z RRFS/ECM/NAM3k reaching or exceeding 4kJ/kg. If 
convective timing aligns with fropa/shortwave passage in the 
afternoon, a significant severe weather signal may be met as 
this aligns with stout deep layer shear, possibly in excess of 
35-45kt. Machine learning severe probs for damaging wind have 
increased for parts of ENC. In addition to the severe threat, 
will have to watch for potential flash flood threat, as PWs 
surge to 2.25" or higher, and with the expected numerous 
convection, very heavy rain rates are possible with deeper 
convection and lend to instances of flash flooding, especially
with potential for training of storms. NBM's deterministicQPF 
values did not tell the whole story by any means, with even the 
bulk of the higher percentile output still advertising less than
one inch over 24h for the entire area. Went with WPC QPF which 
shows a 24h total QPF of 1-2" for areas adjacent to the mouth of
the Neuse River, which the bulk of guidance is showing has the 
best chances of seeing training storms. As a deterministic 
forecast, this will suffice, but there is absolutely potential 
for 24h rainfall totals in excess of 2-3" in spots.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Behind the front, temperatures and humidity 
will finally get knocked down closer to normal for early 
September, with more comfortable conditions lasting into early 
next week. Still some residual moisture lingering on Sunday and
may see some sct showers, but overall trend is for drier esp as
we begin the work week with pops less than 20% lasting through
mid week. Highs in the mid 80s with lows in the 60s is fcst and
